label: SLA policy
description: Service-level targets on the records of one entity, such as response and resolution for tickets. Each target is a clock that starts, pauses and stops on conditions over the record, with a goal chosen by condition (usually by priority) and measured in the business hours of a calendar or around the clock. The platform warns when a target is at risk and records a breach when it passes its goal; both are platform events (platform.sla.warning, platform.sla.breached). Running clocks keep the goal and calendar they started with, so changing a policy never rewrites history.
usage: Typical targets: response (starts on create, stops when someone picks the record up) and resolution (pauses while waiting on the customer, stops when resolved, resumes if reopened).
Order goals from the most specific (record.priority == 'p1') to a last goal without a condition.
Measure urgent goals around the clock (calendar 24x7) and the rest in business hours.
constraints: id is unique; tenant policies start with tenant__. Default policies can be changed or disabled, not removed.
1–5 targets per policy; target IDs are snake_case; stop is required; onReopen is resume, restart or none.
Goals are 1 minute to 1 year; calendars must exist (or be 24x7); warnAtPercent is 1–99.
Conditions are expressions over record (and prior).

binding.description: Configuration object in a layer's spec catalog; not a layout node.

accessibility.keyboard: Not rendered directly; the SLA panel (activity.sla) shows a record's timers.
